meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the V-1 unit
meta.scope: From the crude charge pumps P-1A/B through the cold preheat (E-1, E-3, E-2, E-14), the desalters V-3 // S-1, the booster pumps P-2A/B and the hot preheat (E-15, E-4 … E-8/E-18), the two-pass fired heater H-1 with its fuel gas and fuel oil systems and EMS UY-105, the transfer line, the 30-tray crude tower V-1 with the MPA and BPA pumparounds, the diesel and AGO strippers V-2A/B, the bottoms pumps P-3A/B, and the overhead E-9/E-10, reflux drum V-4 and off-gas; utilities: steam, cooling, instrument air, power.
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: Design case: 218.75 m³/h of light crude (33 000 bbl/d); heater outlet 388 °C; tower top 136 °C; reflux drum 13.8 kPa g. Trained operators. Risk matrix and target event frequencies are those of the OTS HAZOP and LOPA tabs (teaching values, CCPS style).
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N1.causes:
P-1A trips and the standby P-1B is not started
tank outlet or suction valve closed
FCV-129 and FCV-130 both closed
N1.cons: Desalters and both heater passes lose flow; with the heater still firing the coils overheat (see N4-01)
N1.notes:
Worked example
LOPA (worked example): rates and IPL rules from the OTS LOPA tab, scenario L1 (loss of flow in a heater pass), for the cause "P-1A trips, P-1B not started" only. Credited: FSL-105A/B (SIF-01/02), independent of a pump stop (PFD 0.0295 from the SRS / LOPA tabs). Not credited: the FIC-114 and pass low-flow alarms, because the model gives about 12 s from the trip point to the assumed tube limit, far below an operator response time. f_unmit = 0.1 × 1 × 0.1 = 0.01 per year; f_mit = 0.01 × 0.0295 = 2.95e-04 per year against TEL 0.001 for S4. For the cause "FT-105A/B reads high" the SIF shares the transmitter and gets no credit: that is why the OTS LOPA tab recommends own SIS flow transmitters (SIF-01R/02R).

N1.dev: More crude than the set point
N1.causes:
FT-114 reads low so FIC-114 drives the flow up
set-point error
N1.cons: Heater at maximum firing, outlet temperature falls; column vapour load up, flooding; off-spec products

N1.dev: Less crude than the set point
N1.causes:
FT-114 reads high
P-1 wear
suction strainer plugged
N1.cons: Pass flows fall towards the trip point; low velocity in the coils speeds up coking

N1.causes:
FCV-129 closes with FCV-130 closed
desalter inlet valve shut
N1.cons: P-1 runs at shut-off: seal overheats and leaks crude; flange leak in the exchanger train

N1.causes:
Cold crude from storage
E-1 fouled
overhead load low at reduced rate
N1.cons: Desalting efficiency falls; salts reach the column and corrode the overhead; heater duty rises

N1.dev: Blocked-in exchanger heated by its hot side
N1.causes: Crude side of E-1 isolated while the overhead vapour still flows
N1.cons: Thermal expansion of trapped crude: gasket or tube failure, crude release

N1.dev: Heavy crude or a water slug from the tank
N1.causes:
Tank switch to heavy crude
tank water bottoms drawn
N1.cons: Desalter emulsion and oil under-carry; water flashing in the heater and column, pressure surge and tray damage

N1.dev: Back-flow through the stopped charge pump
N1.causes: P-1A trips while P-1B runs and its check valve passes
N1.cons: Pump spins backwards, seal damage and a small leak

N1.dev: Salts, H₂S or sediment above design in the crude
N1.cons: Fouling of the cold train, overhead chloride corrosion

recs.text: Add a low-flow alarm on P-1A/B discharge and auto-start of the standby pump; at present loss of a charge pump is seen only on FIC-114.
Train every panel operator on the dynamic-check scenarios of this study in the OTS and record the response times.
Make FSL-105A/B independent of the control transmitters FT-105A/B (separate flow elements, or 2oo3 voting).
Confirm thermal relief on every exchanger side that can be blocked in while the other side is hot (E-1 … E-14, E-15 … E-8/E-18); add to the relief study.
Overhead corrosion control: boot-water pH and chloride monitoring, neutraliser and inhibitor injection, exchanger tube-leak sampling.
Water management: drain condensate from steam lines before use, steam traps at low points, dewater crude tanks; procedure for water in a hot column.
